page: Amazon Web Services c8ib.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor operating at a clock frequency of 3.9 GHz. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory totals 64.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs included.

The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring workloads to rely on external network-attached volumes for persistent data needs. Network throughput features a baseline network bandwidth of 33 Gbps to support data transfers between instances and remote storage arrays. The system configuration includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From an architectural standpoint, the 1:2 memory-to-core ratio prioritizes high clock speed and core availability over large memory footprints. By eliminating local storage overhead and pairing 32 vCPUs with 33 Gbps networking, the instance balances compute throughput against externalized I/O. This configuration fits compute-intensive workloads such as batch processing, code compilation, media encoding, and distributed compute jobs.
